la:verb:laudo.html:
laudo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
laus
,
to praise, laud, commend, extol, eulogize, approve (cf.: celebro, praed co).
Lit.
In gen.: omnes mortales sese laudarier optant, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 551 Vahl.): coram in os te laudare,to praise to one's face,; cf.: in faciem,: vituperare improbos asperius, laudare bonos ornatius,,

9, 35: et efferre aliquid,: rationem,: sententiam alicujus,: laudantur exquisitissimis verbis legiones,: legem ipsam,: magnifice,: agricolam laudat juris peritus,praises him as happy, extols his happiness,; so, diversa sequentes,; 109: volucrem laudamus equum, praise as swift, i. e. for swiftness, : laudatur dis aequa potestas,.—Part. as subst.: prava laudantium sermo,.—Pass. with dat.: numquam praestantibus viris laudata est in una sententia perpetua permansio,: Germanicus cunctis laudatus,by all,: herba laudata Eratostheni,: laudataque quondam ora Jovi,.—*

Poet., with object.-gen.: laudabat leti juvenem,pronounced him happy on account of his death,.—
With in and abl.: in quo tuum consilium nemo potest non maxime laudare,: juvenes laudari in bonis gaudent,: scriptores iamborum saepe in illis laudantur,.—
Pass. with inf. (poet.): extinxisse nefas Laudabor,.—(ε) With quod: quod viris fortibus honos habitus est, laudo,: laudat Africanum Panaetius, quod fuerit abstinens,: jamne igitur laudas, quod de sapientibus alter Ridebat, etc.,: non laudans, quod non in melius, sed in deterius, convenitis,.—(ζ) With quoniam: utrumque laudemus, quoniam per illos ne haec quidem genera laude caruerunt,.—(η) With cum (very rare): te quidem, cum isto animo es, satis laudare non possum,: jam id ipsum consul laudare, cum initiatam se (Hispala) non infitiaretur,.—(θ) With si: consilium laudo artificis, si munere tanto Praecipuam in tabulis ceram senis abstulit orbi,.—
In partic.
To pronounce a funeral oration over a person: quem cum supremo ejus die Maximus laudaret,; .—
In medicine, to recommend as a remedy: apri cerebrum contra serpentes laudatur,; .—
To praise, compliment, i. e. dismiss with a compliment, leave, turn from (poet.): laudato ingentia rura, Exiguum colito,: cf.: probitas laudatur et alget,—
Transf., to adduce, name, quote, cite a person as any thing: laudare significat priscā linguā nominare appellareque,; cf.: laudare ponebatur apud antiquos pro nominare, Paul. ex Müll.: id ut scias, Jovem supremum testem laudo,: quem rerum Romanarum auctorem laudare possum religiosissimum,: auctores,; cf.: ut auctoribus laudandis ineptiarum crimen effugiam,: auctore laudato, Cod. 8, 45, 7.—Hence, laudātus, a, um, P. a., extolled, praiseworthy, esteemed, excellent: laudari a laudato viro,; Naev. ap. : omnium laudatarum artium procreatrix,: hunc ubi laudatos jactantem in sanguine vultus videt,: olus laudatum in cibis,.— Comp.: saccharon et Arabia fert, sed laudatius India,.—Sup.: laudatissimus caseus,: virgo laudatissima formae dote,.—Hence, adv.: laudātē, laudably, admirably: regias domos laudatissime ebore adornans, (al. lautissime).

laurĕātus, a, um, adj.
laurea

la:noun:laus.html:
laus, laudis (
gen. plur. laudium, ), f.
for claus, from clavid, kindred to cluo and the Greek κλέϝος
, praise, commendation, glory, fame, renown, esteem (cf.: gloria, praeconium, elogium).
Lit.: in laude vivere,: ut is cum populo Romano et in laude et in gratia esse possit,: cum te (omnes) summis laudibus ad caelum extulerunt,: divinis laudibus ornare aliquem,: Bruti nostri cotidianis assiduisque laudibus, quas ab eo de nobis haberi permulti mihi renuntiaverunt, commotum istum aliquando scripsisse ad me credo,: laude afficere aliquem,: omni laude cumulare,: summam alicui laudem tribuere,: illustri laude celebrari,: maximam laudem ex re aliqua sibi parere,: ornare aliquem suis laudibus et onerare alienis,: aliquem laudibus efferre,: neque ego hoc in tua laude pono,,

91, § 212. Fabio laudi datum est, quod pingeret,: eloquentiae, humanitatis,: brevitas laus est interdum in aliqua parte dicendi, in universa eloquentia laudem non habet,: laudis titulique cupido,: supremae laudes,i. e. a funeral oration,: vitiatam memoriam funebribus laudibus reor,. —

Transf.
A praiseworthy thing, a ground for praise, a laudable or glorious action, a laudable enterprise; a merit, desert, : abundans bellicis laudibus,: nostras laudes in astra sustulit,: summa laus tua et Bruti est, quod exercitum praeter spem existimamini comparasse,: cum ceteris tuis laudibus, hanc esse vel maximam, quod, etc.,: magna laus, et grata hominibus, unum hominem elaborare, etc.,: Suevi maximam putant esse laudem, vacare agros, etc.,: Pericles hac laude (dicendi) clarissimus fuit,; ; : conferre nostris tu potes te laudibus?: conscientia laudis,worth, desert,, epil. 11: te censeri laude tuorum noluerim,.—
Of things, estimation, worth, value, repute (post-Aug.): Cois amphoris laus est maxima,: coccum Galatiae in maxima laude est,: peculiaris laus ejus, quod fatigato corpori succurrit,: Creticae cotes diu maximam laudem habuere,.

la:noun:laudatio.html:
laudātĭo, ōnis, f.
laudo
,
a praising, praise, commendation; a eulogy, panegyric.
In gen.: quam lauream cum tua laudatione conferrem? with your eulogy, i. e. that pronounced by you, : felicitatem ipsam deorum immortalium judicio tribui laudationis est,: quae quidem laudatio hominis turpissimi mihi ipsi erat paene turpis,: in omnibus laudationibus,.—With object.-gen.: laudationes eorum, qui sunt ab Homero laudati,: legis,: laudationes modulatae,songs of praise,.—
In partic.
In a court of justice, a favorable testimony to a person's character, a eulogy, panegyric: lectissimos viros cum legatione ad hoc judicium, et cum gravissima atque ornatissima laudatione miserunt,; ; : judicialis,.—
A funeral oration, eulogy: funebris,; : est in manibus laudatio, quam cum legimus, etc.,: nonnullae mortuorum laudationes,.—With object.-gen.: matronarum,.

la:adj:laudabilis.html:
laudābĭlis, e, adj.
laudo
,
to be praised, praiseworthy, laudable (class. and freq.).
Lit.: laudabile est, quod conficit honestam et praesentem et consequentem commemorationem,: honestum, etiam si a nullo laudetur, natura esse laudabile,: vita,: orationes,; cf. oratores,: vir erga rempublicam, Treb. Poll. Trig. Tyr. 32, 2: civis,; : carmen,: fides,: in Rutilo luxuria est: in Ventidio laudabile nomen sumit,.— As subst.: laudābĭle, is, n., the praiseworthy, .—Comp.: vitae ratio laudabilior,: (voluptas) melioremne efficit aut laudabiliorem virum?fin: multo modestia post victoriam, quam ipsa victoria, laudabilior,.—
Transf., valuable, precious, excellent (post-Aug.): mel,: terra,.—Comp.: laudabilius vinum,.— Hence, adv.: laudābĭlĭter, in a praiseworthy manner, praiseworthily, laudably, ad recte, honeste, laudabiliter, postremo ad bene vivendum, : laudabiliter ac placabiliter propitiandi judices,by flattering expressions,.— Comp.: laudabilius,ext.; 5, 4, 3.—Sup. of the adj. and adv. appear not to occur.

lautĭtĭa, ae, f.
lautus
,
elegance, splendor, magnificence in one's style of living, in one's house, furniture, food, etc.
In gen., : fama ad te de mea nova lautitia veniet,: esse in lautitiis,: accuratissimae lautitiae,: summa cenarum lautitia,: lautitiae causa,: munditiarum lautitiarumque studiosissimus,: lautitia, epularum magnificentia, Paul. ex Müll.—
Lautitia farina appelabatur ex tritico aqua consperso, Paul. ex Müll.

la:noun:laurus.html:
laurus, i (
gen. laurūs, ; ; codd.; abl. lauru, ; but lauro,; nom. plur. laurus, ; acc. plur. laurus, ; ; gen. plur. lauruum, acc. to P.), f.
cf. Germ. lor- in Lorbeere
, a bay-tree, laurel-tree, laurel, sacred to Apollo; cf.: aliquid cedo Qui vicini hanc nostram augeam aram Apollinis. Da sane hanc virgam lauri,; it grew in greatest beauty on Parnassus, and hence is called Parnasia laurus,; its branches were the decoration of poets,; of the flamens,; . In festivals, the ancestral images were decorated with laurel, . The leaves, when eaten, were said to impart the power of prophesying, ; . Victorious generals, in triumphal processions, wore laurel crowns on their heads and carried laurel branches in their hands, while their lictors bore fasces bound with laurel, ; . Before the gate of the imperial palace stood two laurel-trees, with oaken crowns, in honor of the emperor, as the vanquisher of foes and the people's preserver: janitrix Caesarum et pontificum, sqq.; . A wet branch of laurel was used in lustrations, to sprinkle the objects to be purified: cuperent lustrari ... si foret umida laurus,; cf. Dict. Antiq. s. v. lustratio.—
Meton. for laurea, a laurel crown, as the sign of a triumph; hence for triumph, victory: incurrit haec nostra laurus non solum in oculos, sed, etc.,: Parthica,: Indica,: Sarmatica,: ornari lauro secunda,.

In gen.: integritatis et elegantiae,: auctores et laudatores voluptatis,: rerum mearum gestarum laudatores,: temporis acti,: derisor vero plus laudatore movetur,: formae,: tuus,.—
In partic.

One who pronounces a funeral oration, ; .

la:adj:laureus.html:
laurĕus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
of laurel, laurel-.
Adj.: vectes laurei,: folia,: corona,: in nitidā laurea serta comā,: oleum,laurel-oil,: ramus,: ramulus,: pira,i. e. that smell like laurel,: cerasa,grafted on laurel,: nemus,.—
Subst.: laurĕa, ae, f.
(Sc. arbor.) The laurel-tree: laurea in puppi navis longae enata,: tum spissa ramis laurea fervidos Excludet ictus,: factis modo laurea ramis annuit,: ex Pannonia,.—
(Sc. corona.) A laurel crown or garland, laurel branch, as the ornament of Apollo, of poets, of ancestral images, of generals enjoying a triumph, and of letters containing news of a victory: te precor, o vates, assit tua laurea nobis,: laureā donandus Apollinari,: cedant arma togae, concedat laurea linguae, Cic. poët. Off. 1, 22, 77: quam lauream cum tua laudatione conferam,. Sometimes victorious generals, instead of a triumphal procession, contented themselves with carrying a laurel branch to the Capitol: de Cattis Dacisque duplicem triumphum egit: de Sarmatis lauream modo Capitolino Jovi retulit,: urbem praetextatus et laurea coronatus intravit,; ; : thyrsus enim vobis, gestata est laurea nobis,: bellorum laureas victori tradens,.—
Trop., a victory, triumph: primus in toga triumphum linguaeque lauream merite,; cf.: parite laudem et lauream,.
